title: Hudson x David weekly
notes_markdown:
### Where things are

- David still finishing UIST camera-ready (due tomorrow); Engelbart work paused until Saturday
- Hudson finished first pass of the problem-statement paragraph without the word "notebook"; David to edit
- Cap table + incorporation docs uploaded to the Surplus folder

### Engelbart scope for the next 3 weeks

- Single-user only; no team features until a pilot asks
- Import first, canvas second — the canvas is useless with nothing in it
- First connectors: Claude + ChatGPT exports, Zotero, local PDFs, Google Drive
- Explicitly not yet: Slack, email, Notion
- Dedupe will matter immediately (same PDF in Zotero and Downloads) — David wants a content hash + title fuzzy match, Hudson worried about false merges

### Metric

- Agreed to report "time to first useful recall" to Lena every Thursday
- Proxy: click-through from a suggested source to the original item, logged with timestamp since connect

### Fundraising

- Marcus Oyelaran call booked for Aug 20
- Prep: one-page memo, no deck yet; be ready for "who pays"
- Hudson takes the pricing hypothesis: individual researcher $15/mo vs. lab license

### Action items

- [ ] David — submit camera-ready Fri, then edit problem paragraph and send to Lena
- [ ] Hudson — draft 1-page memo for Marcus by Tue
- [ ] David — sketch repo layout (web app, importer workers, shared types) over the weekend
- [ ] Both — 20 researcher names in the shared sheet by Aug 31

transcript.text: Okay recording. Is it — yeah it's going. You look destroyed.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: I'm fine. I'm fine. It's the camera-ready. The ACM template is fighting me on the figure captions.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Is that due today or tomorrow?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Tomorrow. Friday. I'm like ninety percent done, it's the stupid stuff now. The copyright block, the, um, the CCS concepts.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Okay so do you want to just do twenty minutes and go back to it?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Yeah, let's do twenty-five. I want to at least agree on scope so I'm not thinking about it all night.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Cool. So first, I sent you the paragraph. The no-notebook paragraph.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: I saw it. I read it on my phone. It's good, it's a little long. You say "context" like four times.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Because it's about context!
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: I know, I know, but Lena's going to — she's going to circle every one. I'll edit it Saturday.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Fine. Second thing, I put the incorporation docs and the cap table in the Surplus folder. The latest cap table, the one with the tabs.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: The one with the SAFE scenarios?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Yeah, that one.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Okay cool. Scope. Can we do scope?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Scope. So my proposal is, for three weeks, single user only. No sharing, no teams. Even though, like, labs are probably who pays eventually.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Agree. Totally agree. I don't want to build permissions before anyone has used the thing.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: And import first.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Import first. The canvas is cool but it's, like, an empty room if nothing's in it. I keep thinking about that — when I open a new tool and it's empty I just close it.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Which connectors though? Because if we say "import everything" we'll do twelve bad ones.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: I wrote a list on the plane. Uh. Claude and ChatGPT exports, because that's where most of the actual thinking is now. Zotero. Local PDFs. Google Drive.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Not Slack?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Not yet. Slack's a mess of permissions. Email too. Notion — I mean I used Notion for like two months this spring and abandoned it, I don't think—
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: People do use Notion though.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Some people. Let's wait until a pilot asks for it. If someone asks, we do it.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Fine. Writing down "Notion when asked."
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: And then the thing I'm actually worried about is duplicates. Because the second you import Zotero and Downloads you have the same PDF twice. I have, like, every paper three times.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: How do you want to dedupe?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Content hash first. If the bytes match it's the same. Then a fuzzy title match for, like, the arXiv version versus the camera-ready.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: That second part scares me. If you merge two things that aren't the same, that's worse than a duplicate. A duplicate is annoying, a wrong merge is lost data.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Yeah. That's fair. Maybe the fuzzy match just suggests, it doesn't merge.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Suggest, don't merge. I like that.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Okay. Um. Metric. Lena said pick one.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Time to first useful recall.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Yeah, and the proxy is the click — when they click a suggested source and open the original. We log the time since they connected.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Seconds since connect, or sessions since connect?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Uh, both? Store the timestamp and we can compute whatever. But report one number.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Report median hours to first click. Fine.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Fine.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Last thing, Marcus. The call's next Thursday, the twentieth.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Do we need a deck?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I don't think so. I think a one-page memo. Lena said he'll ask who pays, and honestly I don't have a great answer.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: What's the — what's your current answer?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Two options. Individual researcher, like fifteen a month. Or a lab license where the PI pays.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: PIs don't pay for anything. I mean. Sorry. Yan would pay for compute, she wouldn't pay for a notebook.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: That's a data point though. That's literally the kind of thing to say on the call.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Yeah. Okay. You draft the memo, I'll read it Tuesday.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Tuesday. And repo stuff?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: I'll sketch the layout this weekend. Web app, the importer workers, and a shared types package so the importers and the app agree on what an item is.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Monorepo?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Probably. Let me think about it Saturday. My brain is in LaTeX right now.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Go finish your paper.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Going. Oh — and the twenty names. Shared sheet, end of the month.
